q: A is a 2 × 3 matrix and B is a 3 × 4 matrix. What is the order of AB?
x: AB is defined because A has 3 columns and B has 3 rows; the product has the rows of A and the columns of B: 2 × 4. It is BA that is not defined (4 columns against 2 rows).

q: A diagonal matrix whose diagonal entries are all equal is called:
x: Such a matrix is kI for some scalar k: a scalar matrix. The identity matrix is the special case k = 1 and the null matrix the case k = 0.

q: For every square matrix A, the matrix A + Aᵗ is:
x: (A + Aᵗ)ᵗ = Aᵗ + (Aᵗ)ᵗ = Aᵗ + A, so A + Aᵗ is symmetric. It is A − Aᵗ that is skew-symmetric. A = I gives 2I, which is not singular, and A = [[1, 1], [0, 1]] gives [[2, 1], [1, 2]], which is not diagonal.

q: A is the row matrix [1, 2, 3] and B is the column matrix with entries 1, 0, −1 from top to bottom. What is AB?
x: AB is 1 × 1: 1·1 + 2·0 + 3·(−1) = 1 + 0 − 3 = −2. Multiplying entry by entry gives [1, 0, −3], which is not matrix multiplication.

q: A = [[0, i], [i, 0]], where i² = −1. What is A²?
x: Row 1 times column 1 is 0·0 + i·i = −1, row 1 times column 2 is 0·i + i·0 = 0, and row 2 gives 0 and −1 in the same way, so A² = [[−1, 0], [0, −1]] = −I. Squaring each entry gives [[0, −1], [−1, 0]].

q: A = [[2, −4], [1, −2]] and I is the 2 × 2 identity matrix. What is (I + A)³?
x: A² = [[4 − 4, −8 + 8], [2 − 2, −4 + 4]] = O. Since I and A commute, (I + A)³ = I + 3A + 3A² + A³ = I + 3A. Direct check: both equal [[7, −12], [3, −5]].

q: P and Q are square matrices of the same order. When is (P + Q)² = P² + 2PQ + Q²?
o: for every such P and Q
x: (P + Q)² = P² + PQ + QP + Q², which equals P² + 2PQ + Q² exactly when QP = PQ. Matrix multiplication is not commutative in general, so it does not hold for every pair; P = Q is only one case where it holds.

q: Every entry in one row of a square matrix is zero. What is its determinant?
o: it cannot be found without the other entries
x: Expand the determinant along the zero row: every term has a factor 0, so the determinant is 0 whatever the other entries are.

q: A is a skew-symmetric matrix of order 3. What is |A|?
x: Aᵗ = −A, so |A| = |Aᵗ| = |−A| = (−1)³|A| = −|A|, hence |A| = 0. The argument needs odd order: the 2 × 2 skew-symmetric matrix [[0, 1], [−1, 0]] has determinant 1.

q: What is the value of the determinant |[[101, 102], [103, 104]]|?
x: Subtract row 1 from row 2 (the value does not change): |[[101, 102], [2, 2]]| = 202 − 204 = −2. Direct check: 101 × 104 − 102 × 103 = 10504 − 10506 = −2.
R₃ − R₂ = (3, 3, 3) = R₂ − R₁, so R₃ → R₃ − 2R₂ + R₁ makes the third row zero and the determinant is 0. By cofactors: 1(45 − 48) − 2(36 − 42) + 3(32 − 35) = −3 + 12 − 9 = 0.

q: What is the determinant of the matrix [[i, 1], [1, i]], where i² = −1?
x: |[[i, 1], [1, i]]| = i·i − 1·1 = −1 − 1 = −2. Using i² = 1 by mistake gives 0.

q: A = [aᵢⱼ] is a 3 × 3 matrix with |A| = 5, and Aᵢⱼ is the cofactor of aᵢⱼ. What is a₁₁A₂₁ + a₁₂A₂₂ + a₁₃A₂₃?
x: Entries of one row multiplied by the cofactors of a different row always add up to 0: the sum is the expansion of a determinant whose first two rows are equal. The value |A| = 5 comes only from entries and cofactors of the same row.

q: a + b + c = 0. What is |[[a, b, c], [b, c, a], [c, a, b]]|?
x: Add columns 2 and 3 to column 1 (the value does not change): every entry of column 1 becomes a + b + c = 0, so the determinant is 0. Check a = 1, b = −1, c = 0: 1(0 − 1) + 1(1 − 0) + 0 = 0.

q: A is an invertible matrix. Which matrix equals (Aᵗ)⁻¹?
x: Aᵗ(A⁻¹)ᵗ = (A⁻¹A)ᵗ = Iᵗ = I, so (Aᵗ)⁻¹ = (A⁻¹)ᵗ: the inverse and the transpose can be taken in either order. (adj A)ᵗ is |A| times this, not equal to it in general.

q: A 3 × 3 matrix A has |A| = 7. What is the rank of A?
x: |A| ≠ 0, so A is non-singular and its echelon form has 3 non-zero rows: the rank is 3. The rank of a 3 × 3 matrix can never be more than 3, so 7 is impossible.

q: What is the inverse of the matrix [[cos θ, sin θ], [−sin θ, cos θ]]?
o: [[cos θ, sin θ], [−sin θ, cos θ]]
x: The determinant is cos²θ + sin²θ = 1, so the inverse is the adjoint: swap the diagonal entries and change the signs of the other two, giving [[cos θ, −sin θ], [sin θ, cos θ]], which is the transpose.

q: For which value of θ is the matrix [[cos θ, sin θ], [sin θ, cos θ]] singular?
x: The determinant is cos²θ − sin²θ = cos 2θ, which is 0 when 2θ = π/2, i.e. θ = π/4. At θ = π/2 it is cos π = −1, and at π/3 and π/6 it is −½ and ½.

q: A = [[1, 0, 2], [0, 3, 0], [1, 0, 1]]. What is the entry in row 1, column 3 of adj A?
x: adj A is the transpose of the cofactor matrix, so its (1, 3) entry is the cofactor C₃₁ = (+1)·|[[0, 2], [3, 0]]| = −6. Taking C₁₃ = |[[0, 3], [1, 0]]| = −3 forgets the transpose. Check: row 3 of A times column 3 of adj A is 1(−6) + 0 + 1(3) = −3 = |A|.

q: A system of linear equations that has at least one solution is called:
x: A system with at least one solution (exactly one or infinitely many) is consistent; a system with no solution is inconsistent. Homogeneous means all the constant terms are zero.

q: In the system AX = B, the coefficient matrix A is non-singular. What can be said about the system?
o: it has the unique solution X = A⁻¹B
it has a solution only if B = O
x: |A| ≠ 0, so A⁻¹ exists, and multiplying AX = B on the left by A⁻¹ gives X = A⁻¹B, the only solution. No solution or infinitely many solutions can happen only when |A| = 0.

q: A father is three times as old as his son. In 10 years he will be twice as old as his son. How old is the son now?
x: f = 3s and f + 10 = 2(s + 10). Substituting gives 3s + 10 = 2s + 20, so s = 10 (and the father is 30). Check: in 10 years 40 = 2 × 20.

q: Gaussian elimination is applied to x + 3y = 5, 2x + y = 0, using R₂ → R₂ − 2R₁ on the augmented matrix. What is the solution?
x: R₂ − 2R₁ turns (2, 1 | 0) into (0, −5 | −10), so y = 2; back-substitution gives x = 5 − 3(2) = −1. Check: −1 + 6 = 5 and 2(−1) + 2 = 0.

q: Cramer's rule is applied to two linear equations in x and y. The coefficient determinant D is 0 but Dₓ ≠ 0. What does this mean?
o: the system has a unique solution
the system has infinitely many solutions
x: Any solution would satisfy D·x = Dₓ, i.e. 0 = Dₓ, which is false, so the system is inconsistent. Infinitely many solutions need D = Dₓ = Dᵧ = 0; a unique solution needs D ≠ 0.

q: The parabola y = ax² + bx + c passes through (1, 2), (2, 3) and (−1, 6). What is c?
x: a + b + c = 2, 4a + 2b + c = 3, a − b + c = 6. First minus third: 2b = −4, so b = −2; second minus first: 3a + b = 1, so a = 1; then c = 2 − 1 + 2 = 3. Check (2, 3): 4 − 4 + 3 = 3.

q: The homogeneous system x + 2y − z = 0, 2x + y + z = 0 has non-trivial solutions. In which ratio are x, y and z?
x: The second equation minus twice the first gives −3y + 3z = 0, so z = y; then x + 2y − y = 0 gives x = −y. The solutions are (−t, t, t), i.e. x : y : z = 1 : −1 : −1. Check (1, −1, −1): 1 − 2 + 1 = 0 and 2 − 1 − 1 = 0.
